research_question: Freeze the WHOLE early policy computation path (shared trunk + early_head, requires_grad=False) and let only late_head and both critics learn, starting model-only from each seed's compliant ROUND60 ep0. Does the restricted policy family preserve initial-value task performance while gaining cost reduction? This is a restricted-family result on one development block, not a global optimality, non-inferiority or deployment claim.

single_structural_intervention.old: accepted ROUND60 partitioned controller: shared Tanh trunk, two independent early/late SEND/SKIP heads routed by ready_step, task-value head and cost-value head on the same trunk; all twelve parameter objects trainable
single_structural_intervention.new: identical five modules and identical routing; trunk and early_head get requires_grad=False (six frozen parameter objects, 5570 scalars); late_head, value_task_head and value_cost_head stay trainable (six objects, 260 scalars)
single_structural_intervention.not_claimed: freezing the trunk is NOT evidence that the R53 critic->trunk gradient isolation was repaired; the R53 critic_input_detached context is still applied around every update exactly as R58/R60 applied it

routing.rule: ready_step = round(f[18]*1000) - round(f[0]); ready_step<=147 -> early_head, >147 -> late_head
routing.not_an_action_rule: early candidates may still SEND and late candidates may still SKIP; no hard send/skip, no extra emission, the sequential budget mask is never bypassed; sampling, greedy, PPO likelihood recomputation and read-only evaluation all call the same routed forward
